[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
James is currently recorded as born in 1719 in County Londonderry and as having died in 1785. These dates and the family placement come from an unsourced inherited tree and have not yet been matched to an original record.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-2917]] is assessed at 23% (uncertain). The inherited Cross/Derry family places James of the 1719 generation under Charles of the 1686 generation. The33-year sequence is feasible and gives a specific selected family, but the Scottish Charles baptism does not establish an Irish adult or name his son James.

Uncertain23%; the supposed migration and both later-family identities lack an inspected bridge. Estimated profile dates cannot independently corroborate the pedigree.

Next useful test: Find one record anchoring the Cross household before extending its Scottish ancestry.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2916 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-2916]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



=== Cross and Derry reconstruction ===

The attached father, [[Glasgow-2917|Charles Glasgow]], is documented as a child baptised on 10 October 1686 at South Leith, Midlothian, Scotland, to John Glesgowe and Margaret Currie.<ref>“Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4J-JJK : accessed 16 September 2021), John Glesgowe in the entry for Charles Glesgowe, 1686.</ref> No inspected record shows that Charles migrated to Cross or elsewhere in County Londonderry, or that he was this James's father.

PRONI's church-register guide lists Derryloran Church of Ireland baptisms only from 1795/1797 and the Cookstown Presbyterian baptism series from 1822 or later.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], Derryloran CR1/114 and MIC1/15/1 and Cookstown Presbyterian entries; consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> These surviving registers are too late to record James's reported 1719 birth. The 1740 religious return does list Glasgow households at Derryloran, but it does not identify this James or Charles.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf “1740 Protestant Householders' Return”], surname transcript, Glasgow entries at Derryloran; accessed 30 August 2026.</ref>

A similarly aged [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow]] appears in a separate Moneymore and emigrant-family reconstruction. No inspected church, deed, probate or migration record establishes that the two James profiles are duplicates or close relatives, or connects this James to Moneymore, Mary Harkness or the documented emigrant family. The [[Space:Glasgow Families of County Londonderry|County Londonderry study]] therefore keeps the identity and relationships unresolved.

The existing father, child and location fields are retained until a sourced replacement can be entered. They should not be treated as proved by the tree links alone. Deeds, estate papers, probate, religious returns and migration records are the appropriate next search.
